res_callout: Caravan: 68× faster (saved to disk, loaded back)
res_box: Caravan saves the chat to disk. LocalAI keeps it only in memory, so a restart means re-reading it.
res_foot:
Restart = stop and start the server again. Caravan's save works for Qwen only so far: Gemma 4 and GPT-OSS use a different
attention design that it can't reload yet. LocalAI's model reload (~4 s) is not counted. First-message bars are Caravan's runs.
deep_foot:
Caravan, LocalAI and llama.cpp use a memory-saving setting for long chats here. exo's Qwen3 30B crashed before this test.
exo reading speeds are approximate. Qwen3 30B needed a single long chat slot to fit in memory.
mem_foot: Highest memory used by each app during the tests (exo: its own peak figure). LocalAI's optional 8 GB prompt cache was switched off.
take: Caravan picks a long Qwen chat back up in 1.2 s after a restart
LocalAI re-reads the whole 16,000-token chat: 80 s. Not yet working for Gemma 4 / GPT-OSS
LocalAI is quick and easy, but it doesn't add speed
Within a hair of Ollama: it runs llama.cpp underneath, like Caravan and Ollama
exo writes fastest on short chats, but struggles with long ones
Fastest writing on all three; slowest at reading long chats and uses the most memory
Qwen3 30B barely fits on a 24 GB Mac mini
18.7–20.4 GB used against a ~19 GB GPU memory limit, whichever app runs it
caveat:
Caveats: one Mac mini, one run per setup. On the short tests Caravan used a memory-saving setting the others didn't.
exo uses a different model format (MLX), so its models aren't byte-for-byte the same.
